ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS:
Ethan Rivera is a 48-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. His presenting illness included cough, feverishness, fatigue, and shortness of breath that had become difficult to manage at home. The treating team determined that inpatient care was appropriate because of the combined respiratory symptoms, reduced ability to maintain usual activity, and need for observation and treatment. He also has hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. These chronic conditions were considered during planning, without evidence in the record of a separate acute problem requiring admission. The principal diagnosis for this hospitalization is community-acquired pneumonia. No additional acute diagnosis was established during the stay. The admission plan focused on treatment of the respiratory infection, support of hydration and rest, monitoring for clinical change, and coordination of a safe transition back to home.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 2 of 20

CHIEF CONCERN:
Mr. Rivera came to the hospital because a worsening cough and breathing discomfort were interfering with sleep and routine activities. He described several days of feeling unwell, with low energy and intermittent feverishness. He was concerned that symptoms were not improving with home rest and wanted further care. His account did not identify a known recent hospital stay or a clear exposure that changed the initial plan. He was able to provide a history and discuss his usual health needs. The team reviewed his symptoms, their course, and the effect on eating, drinking, sleep, and mobility. The primary concern remained an acute respiratory infection consistent with community-acquired pneumonia. His established diagnoses of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism were recorded as relevant background for inpatient care and discharge planning.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 3 of 20

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The illness began with cough and general malaise, then progressed to greater fatigue and shortness of breath during ordinary activity. Mr. Rivera reported feverishness but did not describe a sudden event or injury. He had attempted rest and fluids at home, without adequate relief. There was no history in the admission account of a recent inpatient stay, and the illness was treated as community acquired. The symptoms prompted evaluation and admission for a period of supervised treatment and observation. The record does not identify a separate source of infection or an additional acute condition. During the stay, the team followed his reported breathing, cough, energy, fluid intake, and ability to resume routine movement. The course gradually improved, allowing a transition to home care with clear precautions and arranged follow-up.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 4 of 20

RELEVANT MEDICAL HISTORY:
Mr. Rivera's known chronic conditions are hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. The admission history included these diagnoses so they could be considered alongside treatment of pneumonia. No additional chronic illness was documented as a major factor in this admission. He described having an established outpatient care routine before becoming ill. The team encouraged him to maintain that routine after discharge and to bring an up-to-date record of his prescribed therapies to follow-up. His diabetes was considered during the acute illness because infection can disrupt usual self-care and appetite. Hypertension and hypothyroidism remained background conditions without a separately documented acute complication. The discharge plan emphasizes routine follow-up for all three conditions and communication with his usual clinician if the illness interferes with ongoing care.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 5 of 20

ADMISSION ASSESSMENT:
At admission, the overall clinical picture was considered consistent with community-acquired pneumonia requiring inpatient treatment. Mr. Rivera's cough, feverishness, fatigue, and breathing discomfort formed the main basis for the working diagnosis and care plan. The team reviewed his ability to manage symptoms at home and concluded that observation and treatment in the hospital were appropriate. His chronic diagnoses were included in planning, particularly with regard to maintaining usual self-care during an acute illness. The assessment focused on respiratory recovery, hydration, rest, and gradual return to activity. No other acute diagnosis became the primary focus during the admission. The team discussed the expected course with Mr. Rivera, including that cough and low energy may linger after the acute infection begins to improve. He participated in planning for home recovery.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 6 of 20

INITIAL TREATMENT PLAN:
The initial plan was to treat the pneumonia with an appropriate antimicrobial course and provide supportive care during the period of greatest symptoms. The team encouraged rest and fluid intake as tolerated, while observing for changes in breathing, cough, energy, and ability to perform routine tasks. Additional respiratory support was available if needed, and the approach was adjusted according to his reported symptoms and overall progress. The team also reviewed how acute illness can affect diabetes self-care and appetite, and encouraged him to follow his established care instructions. His chronic conditions were kept in view without introducing a separate acute treatment goal during this stay. Discharge planning began early, with attention to completion of the prescribed course, recovery at home, warning signs, and timely contact with his usual clinician.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 7 of 20

HOSPITAL COURSE, DAY ONE:
On the first hospital day, Mr. Rivera began inpatient treatment for community-acquired pneumonia. His cough, fatigue, and breathing discomfort remained the focus of care. The team provided antimicrobial treatment and supportive measures, with rest and fluids encouraged as tolerated. He was observed for changes in symptoms and for his ability to move about and manage basic needs. The plan accounted for his hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism, while avoiding disruption of his established outpatient care where possible. Mr. Rivera was able to communicate concerns and take part in discussions about the expected course. He was advised that improvement might be gradual and that tiredness or cough could continue after leaving the hospital. Discharge was not planned until symptoms and home-care needs were suitable for outpatient management.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 8 of 20

On the second hospital day, Mr. Rivera reported gradual improvement in breathing comfort and general energy. The cough continued, but it was less disruptive to rest and routine movement. His chronic diagnoses remained stable in the overall care plan, with attention to continuing his usual self-care as his appetite and activity returned. Discussion focused on the anticipated transition to home and the importance of completing the full prescribed course. Mr. Rivera asked appropriate questions about lingering cough and fatigue. The team explained that these symptoms can resolve over time and reviewed the circumstances that would warrant prompt reassessment.

Because illness can affect food intake, activity, and diabetes self-care, he was advised to return gradually to his customary routine and to seek guidance if he could not do so. He was also encouraged to keep a record of his ongoing prescribed therapies and share it at follow-up. The discharge plan does not replace routine care for his chronic conditions. He should contact his usual clinician about any concern that the infection or recovery is interfering with management of hypertension, diabetes, or hypothyroidism.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 11 of 20

CONSULTATIONS:

Mr. Rivera was able to discuss his symptoms, ask questions, and participate in decisions about home recovery. The team determined that specialty input was not needed to establish a safe discharge plan. His usual outpatient clinician remains the appropriate point of contact for continued management of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism after recovery from the acute illness. If his course changes or a new concern arises, the outpatient clinician may determine whether additional expertise is appropriate. No separate specialist recommendation or pending specialty plan was documented at discharge. The primary focus remained completion of pneumonia treatment, symptom recovery, and timely follow-up.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 12 of 20

PROCEDURES:
No procedure was performed during this hospitalization. Mr. Rivera received treatment and observation for community-acquired pneumonia, with care directed toward symptom improvement and a safe return home. There was no procedural recovery period or device care requirement to continue after discharge. The absence of a procedure simplifies the home plan, which centers on completing the prescribed pneumonia treatment, resting, maintaining fluids as tolerated, and gradually resuming normal activity. Mr. Rivera was encouraged to contact his clinician if a new issue develops or if symptoms worsen rather than attempting to manage a change without guidance. There are no procedure-related restrictions in the discharge instructions. His ongoing care for hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism should continue according to the guidance already provided by his outpatient clinicians.

COMPLICATIONS AND PENDING ISSUES:
No major complication was documented during the admission. Mr. Rivera's symptoms improved with inpatient treatment and supportive care, and no additional acute diagnosis became a focus of care. A residual cough and fatigue remained at discharge, with expectation of gradual recovery at home. No pending inpatient intervention was identified as necessary before leaving the hospital. He can increase walking and other ordinary activities gradually, using symptoms as a guide and pausing when tired or short of breath. As appetite improves, he should return to the eating pattern recommended for his type 2 diabetes mellitus and follow his established self-care guidance. If poor intake continues or he cannot maintain fluids, he should contact his clinician. No special diet or procedure-related restriction was established for this admission. The goal is a steady return to customary routines without worsening respiratory symptoms or disrupting care of his chronic conditions.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 15 of 20

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
The principal discharge diagnosis is community-acquired pneumonia, improved after inpatient treatment. Additional established diagnoses are hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. No other acute diagnosis was documented as requiring continued hospital care. Mr. Rivera is leaving with a plan to complete the prescribed pneumonia treatment and continue supportive care at home. A residual cough and fatigue may persist during recovery, but he was able to participate in planning and understood the need to watch for worsening symptoms. His chronic conditions remain appropriate for ongoing outpatient management. The discharge diagnoses are intended to guide follow-up and do not replace review by his usual clinician. He should provide the discharge information to that clinician so the recovery plan and his established care can be considered together.
Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 16 of 20

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
At discharge, Mr. Rivera reported meaningful improvement in breathing comfort, energy, and ability to manage routine activity compared with the beginning of admission. He was able to understand the plan, describe when to seek help, and participate in arrangements for follow-up. No new acute concern was identified that required continued inpatient care. Ethan Rivera | MRN-55529 | Discharge summary | Page 17 of 20

Mr. Rivera should complete the prescribed antimicrobial course for pneumonia exactly as directed in his discharge instructions. Rest, fluids as tolerated, and gradual return to activity remain important parts of recovery. He should keep his discharge paperwork available and share it with his usual clinician. Mr. Rivera should rest as needed, drink fluids as tolerated, and increase activity gradually. Mr. Rivera should arrange follow-up with his usual outpatient clinician after discharge to review recovery from pneumonia and ongoing care for hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. He should contact the clinic sooner if breathing, cough, energy, appetite, or ability to manage daily care worsens rather than waiting for the planned appointment. If symptoms continue to improve, he should still attend follow-up as arranged. DISPOSITION AND CLOSING SUMMARY:
Mr. Rivera was discharged home after an inpatient stay for community-acquired pneumonia. He improved with treatment and supportive care and was considered able to continue recovery outside the hospital. A residual cough and fatigue may persist, but worsening symptoms or failure to improve should prompt contact with a clinician. His hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism remain part of his ongoing outpatient care. He understands the discharge instructions and follow-up plan. The discharge information should be shared with his usual clinician to support continuity of care and a safe return to his normal routine.

If he develops worsening abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, inability to drink, feverishness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or a concerning change at an incision, he should not wait for routine follow-up. He should seek urgent evaluation. If he has questions about diet, activity, or recovery before the scheduled appointments, he may contact the surgical team for guidance.
